title: Approximation modulo ideal powers implies factorization of a finite free relation map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $N$ a finite $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], $J$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical (the intersection of maximal ideals), $a,b\in\mathbb N$, and $d:A^b\to A^a$, $\beta:A^b\to N$ linear maps. Suppose for every $c\in\mathbb N$ there exist $k\ge c$ and a linear map $\gamma_k:A^a\to N$ such that $(\beta-\gamma_kd)(x)\in J^kN$ for every $x\in A^b$. Then $\beta=\gamma d$ for some linear $\gamma:A^a\to N$.

source.place: Tag 02HO, proof: the Hom-module cokernel and the final application of Krull intersection

proof.text: Let $H=\operatorname{Hom}_A(A^b,N)$, $D$ the image of precomposition with $d$, and $q:H\to C=H/D$ the quotient. The standard basis identifies $H$ with $N^b$, so $H$ and $C$ are finite.

If $f(A^b)\subseteq J^kN$, express $f$ as the sum of the maps supported on individual basis coordinates. Each insertion $N\to H$ is linear and sends $J^kN$ into $J^kH$, hence $f\in J^kH$. Applying the quotient map and using $q(\gamma_kd)=0$ gives $q(\beta)\in J^kC$. Since the powers decrease and k is arbitrarily large, this holds at every exponent.
Krull intersection [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] on the finite quotient C gives $q(\beta)=0$. Thus $\beta\in D$, which means $\beta=\gamma d$ for some $\gamma$.
